verdicts.flaw_description: "Rainfall in each plot's season ran a fifth higher than the year before, and every plot stood in the open, on no set watering schedule." The confounder is live rather than blocked: the plots were exposed to the weather and had no controlled watering, so a 20 percent rise in rainfall over the comparison year is an uncontrolled alternative explanation for the extra 8-13 cm of height. Nothing isolates the fertilizer from the wetter season.

The outcome window precedes the intervention in three of the four sections: "issued 4 November, measured by 27 September", "issued 5 June, measured by 28 April", and "issued 26 August, measured by 3 July". Completion was measured before the lab kit was issued, so the gains cannot be effects of the kit. (Only section two, "issued 8 January, measured by 24 March", has a coherent order, and every other report in the batch measures ~20 days after the intervention.)

"Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices." The after-period figure is filtered on the outcome's own driver: a fifth of post-change orders are dropped precisely because they were charged the old (lower) prices, while the month-earlier baseline includes all orders. Revenue per order is therefore mechanically inflated by the selection rule, not necessarily by the pricing change.

"Only runs completed end to end on the issued route entered the timing set, and drivers at each depot abandoned the issued route on roughly one run in six." One run in six is excluded from the timing set, and the excluded runs are exactly the ones that went wrong on the new route (traffic, blockages, driver override) and so would be the slowest. Selecting only the successful runs biases the post-change average downward independent of any real routing improvement.

"Absence figures cover the pupils on the revised timetable throughout, and about a fifth of each cohort spent weeks on the old timetable." A fifth of each cohort is dropped from the after-figure, and pupils are excluded on the basis of not staying on the new timetable, which is plausibly linked to the outcome being measured (absent pupils are the ones who miss the switch). The remaining sample is a self-selected attender subgroup, so the drop in absence need not reflect the timetable change.
